subject: Unbilled tokens on July invoice + proposal for redistribution
messages:
From: Ben Liao <ben.liao@vaulthealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unbilled tokens showing on July invoice — need clarification

Hi Grace,

We've been reconciling our July invoice and I see ~18k tokens marked as 'unbilled/redistributable' in the line items. Can you help explain: which requests those came from, why they weren't applied to prior committed buckets, and whether we can move them into the current month's committed units? Our procurement team is sensitive to rounding effects and minimums when reconciling POs.

A couple of specifics that would help:
- Are partial-token rounding decisions applied per request or per session?
- How do long-context API calls (20k+ context) split across billing units — are those charged as multiple tokens buckets or as one large request?
- If we accept a 10% committed discount this quarter, can you apply any leftover tokens toward next month (or convert to a credit)?

We're close to issuing a PO for the quarterly commit once we understand the accounting. Please loop in whoever can confirm the technical meter behavior.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Liao
Head of Platform Integrations
VaultHealth

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Liao <ben.liao@vaulthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unbilled tokens showing on July invoice — need clarification

Hi Ben — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the confusion. I dug into the line items and attached a short proposal (billing-redistribution-proposal.pdf) that shows your options and the team recommendation. Key points: 

- Origin: the ~18k tokens are from a mix of long-context batch ingestion jobs we received on 2025-07-08 and a set of ephemeral streaming calls where the session heartbeat did not qualify for prefix reuse. Those two patterns prevent automatic carry-forward into prior committed buckets under our current amortization rule.
- Rounding / partial tokens: our default meter rounds up partial tokens per API call to the nearest 8-token quantum to avoid undercounting micro-requests. That means small spikes can inflate counts; see proposal page 2 for sample math.
- Long-context (20k+): those are split into 16k/4k internal model chunks at serving time; billing will show two invoice lines unless you enable 'context-tiling aggregation' (we can toggle at the account level). Aggregation reduces line items and lets the platform amortize across the request window.

Proposal (short):
1) Move up to 15k of the unbilled tokens into July's committed bucket as a one-time redistribution (no price change).
2) For the remaining ~3k, issue a credit to be consumed in August or keep as a rolling credit (your choice).
3) As a commercial concession for the churn you experienced, I'll offer a one-time supplemental discount of 6% on July invoice if you sign the attached PO by 2025-07-27.

Next steps: if that sounds reasonable I'll loop in Karthik to confirm the meter toggles (context-tiling aggregation) and documentation we'll include in the SOW appendix. Can we aim to finalize by next Monday?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: billing-redistribution-proposal.pdf (6 pages; summary + worked examples)

From: Ben Liao <ben.liao@vaulthealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unbilled tokens showing on July invoice — need clarification

Hi Grace — thanks for the quick write-up, that helps a lot. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering: 

- The rounding to 8-token quanta is the main driver for our discrepancy. Can you confirm whether that quantum is configurable per account (say, reduce to 4 tokens) or fixed in the platform? If configurable, what are the performance or cost trade-offs?
- For the context-tiling aggregation toggle: does enabling it change how we count prefix/KV cache reuse across separate calls with the same conversation_id? Our ingestion job uses many parallel workers that share prefixes; we need assurances the aggregated accounting won't double-count across workers.
- On the discount: VaultHealth is pushing to standardize on a 12% committed discount for this quarter given expected volume. If we accept your redistribution proposal, would Redwood be open to 10% (instead of 6%) if we commit to the quarterly PO and sign by 7/27?

I've attached our draft PO (PO_4012.pdf) which references the RDW-2389 deal. If you can confirm the meter behavior and the quantum configurability, procurement can move fast.

Thanks,
Ben

Attachment: PO_4012.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Liao <ben.liao@vaulthealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unbilled tokens showing on July invoice — need clarification

Hi Ben — Karthik on infra/metrics here, copying Marissa for commercial. I wanted to answer the two technical asks so you have something concrete for procurement: 

1) Quantum configurability: the default 8-token quantum is configurable at the account level but is gated behind a per-deal performance review. Moving to a smaller quantum (4 tokens) decreases per-request rounding overhead but increases metering cardinality (more invoice lines) and can slightly increase pipeline CPU pressure during high-concurrency ingestion. For VaultHealth volumes the delta is minimal; we can provision the metering pipeline for 4-token quantum with no change to serving SLOs.

2) Context-tiling aggregation & prefix reuse: enabling aggregation will make the billing layer attempt to coalesce tiles that share the same conversation_id and identical KV-cache keys within the aggregation window (default: 45s). It will not merge across independent conversation_ids or across workers that do not share KV keys. In your ingestion pattern (parallel workers that reuse prefixes), aggregation will reduce double-counting as long as the workers write identical prefix keys; if they generate independent prefixes, aggregation won't coalesce them. We can add a short instrumentation step in your pipeline to ensure prefixes are deduped before upload — we can provide a script for that.

3) Long-context split behavior: when we tile a 20k request into 16k+4k, billing will default to two invoice lines. With aggregation enabled and if tiles are sequential with shared prefixes, the billing layer will amortize some KV-cache tokens and reduce effective billable tokens by up to ~3-7% depending on reuse. Exact savings are in the attached Drive appendix.

Commercial note (re: discount): if VaultHealth signs the PO by 2025-07-27 and enables aggregation, Redwood can accept 10% committed discount for the quarter, provided the account also agrees to the 4-token quantum toggle for the duration of the quarter. We'll document the change in the SOW appendix and include a sample reconciliation script. Grace / Marissa — I'll prepare the appendix and the toggles so we can ship this as amendment to RDW-2389.
